q: What is Suwaya and what is its core concept?
a: Suwaya is an open-source Astro-Productivity application designed to reconnect your daily rhythm, tasks, and focus sessions with solar movement and prayer times at your geographic location, rather than relying solely on rigid civil clock hours.

q: What is a 'Suwaya' and how does the 24-Suwaya system work?
a:
Instead of dividing the day into 24 equal civil hours starting at midnight, Suwaya divides the astronomical day (from Maghrib to the next Maghrib) into 24 Suwayas across two phases:
• Night Phase (🌑): Extends from Maghrib to Sunrise and consists of 12 Night Suwayas (numbered 01 to 12).
• Day Phase (☀️): Extends from Sunrise to the next Maghrib and consists of 12 Day Suwayas (numbered 01 to 12).
Each Suwaya consists of 60 virtual minutes (written as 00|00), while its real duration expands or contracts according to the length of night and day in your season and location.

q: Why does the day in Suwaya start at Maghrib instead of midnight or Fajr?
a: The app follows the authentic astronomical and Islamic calendar cycle where night precedes day; a new day begins at sunset (Maghrib). Therefore, you will see headers like 'Night of Friday' after Maghrib, which then transitions to 'Day of Friday' after Fajr.

q: What are the seven astronomical periods of the day?
a:
The dial divides the cycle from Maghrib to the next Maghrib into 7 contiguous periods without gaps:
1. Maghrib Period (Maghrib to Isha).
2. Isha Period (Isha to astronomical midnight) — shares 5 Night Suwayas with the Maghrib period.
3. Second Half of the Night / Qiyam Period (Astronomical midnight to Fajr) — fixed at 6 Night Suwayas (06|00 🌑 to 11|59 🌑).
4. Fajr Period (Fajr to Sunrise) — fixed at 1 Night Suwaya (Suwaya 12 🌑).
5. Duha Period (Sunrise to Dhuhr).
6. Dhuhr Period (Dhuhr to Asr).
7. Asr Period (Asr to next Maghrib) — the 12 Day Suwayas (01 ☀️ to 12 ☀️) are dynamically distributed across the Duha, Dhuhr, and Asr periods.

q: What does the Time Flow Speed indicator (e.g., 1.25x or 0.85x) mean?
a:
Since each Suwaya represents 60 virtual minutes (3,600 virtual seconds) while its real duration varies by period and season, the speed indicator shows how fast virtual Suwaya minutes flow compared to civil minutes:
• 1.00x: 1 Suwaya equals exactly 60 civil minutes.
• Greater than 1.00x (with lightning icon ⚡): The period is short, so Suwaya minutes flow faster than civil minutes.
• Less than 1.00x (with hourglass icon ⏳): The period is long and extended, so Suwaya minutes flow more calmly and slowly than civil minutes.

q: How do I read Suwaya time and how does it differ visually from civil time?
a:
Suwaya time is designed to be recognizable at a glance:
• Suwaya time is always displayed in Astro Gold and uses a vertical bar (|) between Suwayas and virtual minutes along with a phase icon, such as (04|30 🌑) for the 4th Night Suwaya and 30 virtual minutes, or (08|15 ☀️) for the 8th Day Suwaya and 15 virtual minutes.
• Civil time is displayed in white/neutral text with a standard colon (:).
You can switch between Suwaya time and civil time globally at any moment by tapping the clock/crescent icon in the top bar.

q: What are the five Qiyam (Night Prayer) parts available in the app?
a:
For Qiyam, the app focuses on Period 3 (Second Half of the Night: from astronomical midnight to Fajr, spanning 6 Suwayas) and provides 5 precise subdivisions:
• Second Half of the Night: 6 Suwayas (06|00 🌑 to 11|59 🌑).
• Last Third of the Night: 4 Suwayas (08|00 🌑 to 11|59 🌑).
• Fourth Sixth of the Night: 2 Suwayas (06|00 🌑 to 07|59 🌑).
• Fifth Sixth of the Night: 2 Suwayas (08|00 🌑 to 09|59 🌑).
• Sixth Sixth of the Night: 2 Suwayas (10|00 🌑 to 11|59 🌑).
The app automatically prevents overlapping selections on the dial to keep the visual layout clean.

q: How do I use the interactive Astronomical Astrolabe Dial on the Home screen?
a:
The astronomical dial is fully interactive:
• Tap: Tap any period ring, prayer marker, task arrow, or routine arc to view a detailed dialog with start/end times (in both civil and Suwaya formats), Suwaya count, and flow speed.
• Manual Rotation: Drag the dial with your finger to explore periods; it will elastically snap back when released.
• Drag & Drop: Long-press any task arrow on the dial, then drag and drop it onto another period or Suwaya to reschedule the task immediately.
• Quick Edit: Tap the (Edit Dial ✏️) button above the dial to toggle Sunrise and Qiyam night parts.

q: What is the difference between Casual Tasks, Continuous Habits, and Routines?
a:
• Casual Tasks: One-time tasks linked to a specific date and time (Suwaya or civil).
• Continuous Habits: Recurring daily or weekly actions that track your completion streaks and include 3 Streak Freezes to protect your progress if you miss a day.
• Routines: Time blocks with a start and end time (such as sleep, work, or study blocks) rendered as colored, patterned arcs (4 geometric patterns) on the astronomical dial.

q: How does the Focus Timer (Suwaya Pomodoro vs. Traditional Pomodoro) work?
a:
The app offers two focus modes:
1. Traditional Pomodoro: Uses standard civil minutes (default 25m work / 5m short break, and a 30m long break every 4 cycles) with Start, Pause/Resume, Skip, and Reset controls, plus a top settings button to customize all durations and cycle counts.
2. Suwaya Pomodoro: Anchors the start time when you enter the setup screen and defaults the end time to the next mandatory prayer (or any custom time between 15 minutes and 12 hours/Suwayas). It divides the interval into an integer number of 25/5 virtual Pomodoros with a flow speed between 0.5x and 2.0x (defaulting to the speed closest to 1.00x), deducts setup time from the first Pomodoro, and stops automatically at prayer time.

q: Does the app require an internet connection to calculate timings or search for cities?
a: No. Suwaya is offline-first; it includes a bundled local database of thousands of cities worldwide. Even when using GPS, it finds your nearest city and configures the calculation method and Madhab automatically without needing internet access.

q: There is a few minutes' difference between the app and my local mosque. How can I adjust it?
a: Open the side drawer, go to (Settings) -> (Astronomical Calculations), where you can change the calculation method, Madhab, or custom angles, or tap (Manual Time Offsets) to adjust any mandatory prayer individually from -30 to +30 minutes.

q: What alert levels are available for prayers, Qiyam, tasks, and routines?
a:
You can configure each item with one of 3 alert levels:
1. Silent: No notifications.
2. Standard Notification: A quiet notification in the system tray.
3. Strong Alarm (Wake Screen): A full-screen alarm that appears over the lockscreen with gradual audio fade-in, supporting swipe-to-stop/snooze as well as hardware volume buttons for snoozing.

q: What happens to my old tasks after updating to the new V2 time system?
a: The app includes an automatic Migration Service that runs on startup; it safely upgrades tasks and routines created under the older model to a fallback civil time (10:00 AM) so none of your tasks are lost, allowing you to reschedule them into your preferred Suwaya.

q: Where is my data stored and what is Suwaya's privacy policy?
a: All your tasks, habits, routines, settings, and saved locations are stored locally on your device inside a fast local database (Isar). Suwaya has no cloud servers and does not collect, track, or share any personal or advertising data.

title: 3. In-App Purchases (Store Billing & RevenueCat)
content: If you choose to purchase or restore a supporter badge, Suwaya uses platform store billing and the RevenueCat SDK to verify your supporter entitlement using an anonymous app user ID and purchase receipt status. Sensitive payment information is processed exclusively by the platform store and is never accessed or stored by Suwaya.

title: 6. Third-Party Libraries and Network Access
content: Suwaya uses open-source Flutter libraries for local persistence, astronomical calculations, and geolocation. Network requests are strictly limited to fetching documentation updates (FAQ and Privacy Policy) from the official GitHub repository, checking for app updates, and verifying supporter purchases via RevenueCat.
